claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to claim for my one child, Alex. Could you help me work out if I'm eligible?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! Of course, I'd be happy to help you work out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me start by asking: how old is Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Since Alex is 16, I have a follow-up question:

Is Alex currently in full-time approved education or training (such as A-levels, T-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or have they recently left education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They left school recently but haven't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex is 16 and has recently left education, I have a couple more questions to help determine your eligibility.

Has Alex registered with their local careers service, Connexions, or a similar training provider? This is sometimes also referred to as registering as someone who is not in education, employment or training (NEET).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with careers service or anything like that yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question:

When did Alex turn 16, or more specifically, when did they leave school? 

The reason I ask is that Child Benefit can continue until the end of February after a child turns 16, or until 31 August after they leave education if that's later. This helps me understand if you might still be eligible for a short period.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex turned 16 a few months ago and left school around the same time - that was back in the summer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Based on what you've told me, here's the situation:

Since Alex:
- Is 16 years old
- Left school in the summer
- Is not currently in approved full-time education or training
- Has not registered with a careers service or similar organisation

Child Benefit would have continued until **31 August** following Alex leaving school. After that date, eligibility would end unless Alex either:
1. Returns to full-time approved education or training, or
2. Registers with a careers service, Connexions, or similar training provider (in which case benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks while they are not in education, employment, or training)

Since we are now past 31 August and Alex hasn't taken either of those steps, I'm afraid you would no longer be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me record this outcome for you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Summary:**
- Alex is 16 and left school in the summer
- Child Benefit continued until 31 August after leaving education
- Since Alex is not in approved full-time education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or similar organisation, eligibility has ended

**However, there are ways you could become eligible again:**

1. **If Alex returns to education or training** – If Alex enrols in approved full-time education (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or similar) or approved training, you could claim Child Benefit again until they are 20 (as long as they remain in qualifying education/training).

2. **If Alex registers with a careers service** – If Alex registers with their local careers service, Connexions, or a training provider, you may be able to claim for up to 20 weeks while they are looking for education, training, or employment.

I hope this helps clarify things. If Alex's circumstances change, you may wish to revisit your eligibility at that time. Is there anything else I can help you with?

reasonings: Alex is 16 years old and left school in the summer. Child Benefit can continue for a child aged 16 until 31 August after they leave education. However, after this date, eligibility only continues if the child is in approved full-time education or training, OR if they have registered with a careers service/Connexions/training provider (which allows benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks while NEET). Since Alex is not in education or training and has not registered with any careers service, the claimant is no longer eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
